name: Word Order
moduleIntroduction: Welcome! This lesson is about Word Order. English and French are similar (Subject-Verb-Object), but the details are different. In French, you say "une voiture rouge" (a car red), but in English, you must say "a red car". Also, English questions need helper verbs like 'do' or 'did'. This module will help you master these patterns.
contrastiveExplanation:
Adjective Placement:
English: Adjective + Noun ("A red car").
French: Noun + Adjective ("Une voiture rouge").

Adverb Position:
English: Before the main verb ("I always go") BUT after 'to be' ("I am always").
French: Usually after the verb ("Je vais toujours").

Question Formation:
English: Auxiliary + Subject + Verb ("Do you like...?").
French: Often uses intonation or "Est-ce que".

Negative Sentences:
English: Auxiliary + Not + Verb ("I do not like").
French: "Ne...pas" around the verb.

commonErrors.wrong: She is wearing a dress green.
commonErrors.correct: She is wearing a green dress.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: French puts colors after the noun ("une robe verte").

commonErrors.wrong: Mr. Foncha is a teacher very good.
commonErrors.correct: Mr. Foncha is a very good teacher.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: English adjectives come before the noun.

commonErrors.wrong: My father goes always to church.
commonErrors.correct: My father always goes to church.

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Adverbs come AFTER the verb 'to be'.
English must use the auxiliary 'Do' for questions.
English must use 'Did' and invert the subject.

commonErrors.correct: I do not (don't) know the answer.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: English needs the auxiliary 'do' for negatives.

commonErrors.wrong: My brother can not to come.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Modals like 'can' are followed by the base verb without 'to'.

items.feedback: Correct! In English, the adjective (red) comes BEFORE the noun (car).
Correct! Adjectives in English never take an 's', even if the noun is plural. And it comes before the noun.
Correct! To make a question in the Present Simple, we start with 'Do'.
Correct! For negative sentences, we need 'Subject + do not + Verb'.

items.feedback: Correct! Adjective (tall) + Noun (man).
Correct! With the verb 'to be', we invert the subject and verb. 'Is your father...?'
Correct! With the verb 'to be', we put 'not' after the verb.
Correct! Adjective (black) + Noun (shoes). Adjectives do not take 's'.
Correct! Questions start with the auxiliary 'Do'.
Correct! Adjective (new) + Noun (phone).
Correct! Adjective (big) comes before Noun (house).
Correct! 'Hungry' is an adjective, so we use 'Are you', not 'Do you'.
Correct! For 'He', we use the negative auxiliary 'does not'.
Correct! Adjectives do not change form.
Correct! For 'She', we start the question with 'Does'.
Correct! Negative of 'to be' is 'are not'.
Correct! Number + Adjective + Noun.
Correct! Subject is 'they', so we use 'Are'.
Correct! Negative Present Simple: Subject + does not + Verb.
Correct! Adjective (blue) before Noun (pen).

items.questionText: I ___ go to the market on Fridays.
items.feedback: Correct! Adverbs of frequency (usually) go BEFORE the main verb (go). "I usually go..."
Correct! Adverbs of frequency go AFTER the verb 'to be'. "He is always..."
Correct! In Past Simple questions, we use 'Did' + Subject + Base Verb.
Correct! After 'didn't', we use the base verb (see), not the past form (saw).
Correct! Adverb (often) comes before the main verb (drinks).
Correct! In questions, the auxiliary (is) comes before the subject (she).
Correct! 'Well' is the adverb. It usually goes at the end of the phrase. "Speaks English well."
Correct! Question word + Auxiliary (does) + Subject (the film) + Verb (start).
Correct! 'Not' goes between the auxiliary (have) and the main verb (finished).
Correct! The modifier 'very' comes before the adjective 'kind'.

items.questionText: We ___ play football in the rain.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Never' is already negative. We don't say 'don't never'. "We never play..."
Correct! Question word (How often) + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you).
Correct! Adjective before noun. Use 'an' because 'interesting' starts with a vowel sound.
Correct! 'Hardly ever' means 'almost never'. It goes before the verb.
Correct! Present Continuous question: Is + Subject + Verb-ing.
Correct! Modal (cannot) + Base Verb (go). No 'to'.
Correct! 'All' goes after the verb 'to be'.
Correct! Past Simple question uses 'Did' + Subject.
Wait, let's fix the options. Correct sentence is "He runs very fast."
Correct! Quantifier (some) + Adjective (fresh) + Noun (vegetables).

items.questionText: Find the error: "Do you know where is the bank?"
items.feedback: Correct! In indirect questions, we do NOT invert the second part. It should be: "Do you know where the bank IS?"

items.questionText: I have ___ money to buy the phone.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Enough' comes BEFORE a noun. (Enough money).

items.questionText: The house is ___ for all of us.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Enough' comes AFTER an adjective. (Big enough).
Correct! Order of adjectives: Opinion (beautiful) -> Color (red) -> Material (leather).
Correct! When a sentence starts with 'Rarely', we invert the subject and auxiliary. (Inversion).
Correct! Indirect question: Question phrase + Subject + Verb. (No inversion).
Correct! 'Almost' modifies 'never', so it comes first.
Correct! Indirect question. Subject (that man) + Verb (is).
Correct! Order: Opinion (expensive) -> Size/Speed (fast) -> Origin (German).

items.questionText: ___ had I arrived when the phone rang.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Hardly' triggers inversion and is used with 'when'. ('No sooner' is used with 'than').
Correct! With phrasal verbs, if the object is a pronoun (it), it MUST go between the verb and the particle.
Correct! Order: Age (old) -> Color (blue) -> Material (cotton).

items.questionText: Not only ___ beautiful, but she is also smart.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Not only' at the start of a sentence triggers inversion.

items.questionText: Find the error: "I asked him where was he going."
items.feedback: Correct! Indirect question error. It should be: "...where he was going."
Correct! Structure: Verb (speaks) + Object (English) + Adverb (fluently). Do not put the adverb between verb and object.
Correct! With a noun object (the light), phrasal verbs can usually be separated or not.

items.questionText: Little ___ that he was in danger.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Little' with a negative meaning triggers inversion. "Little did he know..."
Correct! We use 'such a' + adjective + noun. (Or 'so' + adjective alone).
Correct! 'I don't think' is followed by a normal statement structure.
Correct! If both objects are pronouns, we usually use: Direct Object (it) + to + Indirect Object (him).
Correct! Adjective (blue) BEFORE Noun (shirt).
Correct! Adjectives never take 's'.
Correct! Present Simple questions start with 'Do'.
Correct! Negative for 'He' is 'does not'.
Correct! Adjective (yellow) + Noun (bird).
Correct! To be verb question: 'Is she...?'
Correct! Negative of 'I am' is 'I am not'.
Correct! Adjective (white) + Noun (teeth). No 's' on adjective.
Correct! Questions start with 'Do'.
Correct! Adjective (good) before Noun (girl).
Correct! Adjective (heavy) before noun.
Correct! 'Tired' is an adjective, so we use 'Is he'.
Correct! Negative Present Simple uses 'do not'.
Correct! Adjectives do not take 's'.
Correct! Question with 'they' starts with 'Do'.
Correct! 'Is not' is the negative of 'is'.
Correct! Number + Adjective + Noun.
Correct! Subject is 'we', so use 'Are'.
Correct! 'Father' is 'he', so use 'does not'.
Correct! Adjective (nice) before Noun (kaba).
Correct! 'Always' goes before the main verb 'eat'.
Correct! Adverbs go AFTER 'is'. "She is always..."
Correct! Past Question: What + Did + Subject + Verb.
Correct! Use base verb 'go' after 'didn't'.
Correct! 'Never' goes before the verb. No double negative.
Correct! Inversion: Are + Subject (you).
Correct! Adverb (carefully) goes after the verb.
Correct! Question word + Auxiliary (does) + Subject (it) + Verb (cost).
Correct! 'Not' goes after the auxiliary 'has'.
Correct! 'Very' comes before 'difficult'.
Correct! 'Rarely' is a negative adverb. "I rarely drink..."
Correct! Question word (When) + Auxiliary (will) + Subject (they).
Correct! Adjective before noun. 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (silent H), so use 'an'.
Correct! 'Seldom' (not often) goes before the verb.
Correct! Present Continuous question: Is + Subject + Verb-ing.
Correct! Modal (must) + not + Base Verb (smoke).
Correct! 'All' goes after the verb 'to be'.
Correct! Past Simple question uses 'Did'.
Correct! Adverb (beautifully) describes the verb (sings).
Correct! Quantifier (some) + Adjective (cold) + Noun (water).

items.questionText: Find the error: "Can you tell me where is the school?"
items.feedback: Correct! Indirect question. It should be: "...where the school IS."
Correct! 'Enough' comes BEFORE the noun (food).

items.questionText: He is not ___ to reach the shelf.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Enough' comes AFTER the adjective (tall).
Correct! Order: Size (big) -> Shape (round) -> Material (wooden).
Correct! 'Never' at the start triggers inversion.
Correct! Indirect question. No inversion.
Correct! 'Almost' modifies 'never', so it comes first.
Correct! Indirect question. Subject (he) + Verb (lives).
Correct! Order: Opinion (beautiful) -> Size/Length (long) -> Color (black).

items.questionText: No sooner ___ the house than it rained.
items.feedback: Correct! 'No sooner' triggers inversion with Past Perfect.
Correct! Phrasal verb with pronoun object (it): Object MUST be in the middle.
Correct! Order: Age (new) -> Color (white) -> Origin (Japanese).
Correct! 'Only later' triggers inversion.

items.questionText: Find the error: "I wonder who is she."
items.feedback: Correct! Indirect question error. Should be: "...who she is."
Correct! Verb + Object + Adverb. Do not put adverb between verb and object.
Correct! With a noun object (shoes), you can separate the phrasal verb or keep it together.
Correct! 'Seldom' triggers inversion.
Correct! 'Such a' + Adjective + Noun.
Correct! Standard statement order after 'I hope'.
Correct! With two pronouns: Direct Object (them) + to + Indirect Object (her).
